findings.title: main admitted a merge while a gate run at the merged head was red by the repository's own platform reader
findings.claim: Of the 52 merges in round 11's window, 1 (#3618) reached main while a check suite at its merged head carried a red latest `gate` run (CI code run 43734029821, gate failed 19:18:44Z, its codeql/Analyze (python) still running and later failed) and 1 (#3644) while a gate re-run was in progress; `merge_train.platform_gate`, documented as GitHub's own required-check evaluation, reads #3618 red, so the ruleset's required `gate` check does not enforce what the train assumes it enforces.
findings.mechanism: main-protect-checks requires the context `gate` (integration 15368). Every ci.yml run (edit, review, code, dispatched code) publishes its own `gate` check run in its own check suite at the head. GitHub admitted the merge with four suites' gates green and the dispatched code run's gate red; the train's platform_gate requires every required gate run to pass. The only refusal of a red-gate merge is therefore client-side (merge_train / merge_pr.sh), which a merge under the owner account outside the train does not pass through.

evidence.unit: merges not green at merged_at (1 red, 1 wait)
evidence.contention_note: other finder seats on the box; counts over fixed snapshots, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb: add FAILURE to merge_train.PLATFORM_PASS (the reader accepts a red gate run)

findings.metric_definition: count of window merges whose merged head, at merged_at, platform_gate reads not green over each check suite's latest gate run completed by then
findings.phenomenon_property: No merge reaches main while any check suite at the merged head carries a red or unfinished latest `gate` run; the platform, not only the train, refuses it.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Make the platform refuse it: either one gate per head (the code run's gate the only check run named `gate`, the others renamed), or a required check whose single run reads every suite at the head; and record in decision 0011/0013 that platform_gate is stricter than GitHub so a non-train merge is not covered.

findings.title: The human oversight point is not provable from GitHub's records: 0 of 52 window merges carry the owner's own approval
findings.claim: In round 11's window, 31 of 52 merges carry an approval at head under the owner's account and all 31 are agent-declared; 0 carry one `budget_raise_gate.approval` reads as the owner's own, 49 of 52 were merged by the owner's account, and the agent/human split is made by review-body text alone (deleting the AGENT_DECLARED words turns all 31 into the owner's own with no GitHub-recorded field changed).
findings.mechanism: Mandate 6893738184 (scope all, decision 0013) lets the orchestrator approve and merge as tvofi. GitHub's record (login, id, type) is identical for the agent and the owner, so the code-owner review that main-protect-checks requires, the only human-in-the-loop point GitHub enforces, is satisfied by an agent; whether a human acted is recoverable only from what the agent wrote, which is the 'comment's word' D11's NIST AI 600-1 bar excludes.

findings.phenomenon_property: Every merge's required human approval is attributable to a human from GitHub-recorded identity, not from body text an agent writes.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: For the owner to rule: a separate GitHub identity for agent approvals under mandate (an App or a machine user listed as code owner only while a mandate is in force) so records alone separate agent from owner; or record per merge an owner act GitHub signs (the owner's own review) at a sampled rate.

findings.title: The release asset users install carries no provenance; the attestation covers the tag tree only
findings.claim: Of the last 5 releases, 0 `heatpump_optimizer.zip` assets (the file hacs.json's zip_release install fetches) have a GitHub attestation for their sha256, while 5 of 5 tag-tree tars (the subject release.yml attests) do; Scorecard Signed-Releases finds 0 of 5 with a signature or provenance asset.
findings.mechanism: release.yml's 'Attest the tag's tree' step sets subject-digest to `git archive --format=tar <tag> | sha256sum`, a serialisation no user downloads; the zip the same job builds and uploads is never a subject. SLSA v1.0 Build L1 asks for provenance of the distributed artifact, so the release path meets L1 (and L2) for an artefact no one installs and L0 for the one installed.

evidence.unit: zip assets attested (of 5 releases; tag tars attested 5)
evidence.contention_note: other finder seats on the box; counts over fixed snapshots, contention-immune

findings.metric_definition: releases (last 5) whose distributed zip asset's sha256 has >=1 attestation via GET /repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/attestations/sha256:<digest>
findings.phenomenon_property: Every release asset a user installs is a subject of a signed build-provenance attestation.

findings.title: Policy mandates stated verbatim in two policy files, and rulings policy already states
findings.claim: Over the 84-file policy set D11.md names, 16 normalized units of >= 8 words occur verbatim in two or more files; 6 of them are live mandates outside the recorded deliberate pair and the decision history (root-cause.md/defect-root-cause.md RCA cost rule; standing-roster.md/standing-tick.md retirement constraint; steward SKILL.md/claim-files.md merge-tree check; D4.md/D4-criteria.md and D5.md/D5-criteria.md owner criteria; D11.md/RULINGS.md mechanise-first), and 1 further live RULINGS.md entry quotes text D6.md states (rulings_overlap=1), against the owner's one-mandate-one-file rule (tvofi 2026-11-15).
findings.mechanism: Nothing measures cross-file restatement: policy_lint's `duplicates` class compares generated copies only, and RULINGS.md's rule (1) 'an entry policy already states is dropped' has no detector, so a mandate copied into a second role, brief or criteria file, or kept in RULINGS after a brief adopts it, stays until an audit reads it.

evidence.unit: duplicate units (>= 8 words) across the policy set; rulings_overlap=1
evidence.contention_note: other finder seats on the box; a count over the tree

perturbation.change: --perturb: delete, in memory, one file's copy of every duplicate unit and every corpus sentence an overlapping ruling quotes

findings.metric_definition: normalized text_ledger D6 units of >= 8 words present in >= 2 policy files (.claude/rules folded onto source), plus live RULINGS entries a corpus file states
findings.phenomenon_property: Each mandate is stated once, in the most authoritative policy file owning it, and pointed to elsewhere; no live RULINGS.md entry is stated by a policy file.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Keep each of the 6 mandates in its owning file and replace the other copy with a pointer; drop the two RULINGS entries D6.md and D11.md state; report CLAUDE.md/orchestrator.md section 8 (recorded deliberate) and the four criteria files' shared provenance sentence to the owner; mechanise: a policy_lint class over text_ledger units refusing a new verbatim cross-file unit.
